subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: Alice Munro and the Story as Novel
description: A 60-second lesson on Alice Munro and the Story as Novel.

hook.text: Alice Munro won the Nobel Prize writing only short stories, proving the form could stand beside the novel.

buildup.text: Her stories span decades within a few pages, compressing entire lifetimes into a single reading experience.

discovery.text: She wrote almost exclusively about small-town Ontario, finding the universal within the intensely local.

twist.text: The Nobel committee called her 'master of the contemporary short story,' a title never before given to the form.

climax.text: Munro proved that a short story can contain as much life, time, and complexity as any thousand-page novel.

punchline.text: She fit entire lifetimes into thirty pages.

quiz.question: Why was Munro's Nobel Prize historically significant?
options: She was the youngest winner ever
It recognized the short story form at the highest level of literary achievement
She won it for a novel, not short stories
